note: The real-history spine: ~200 curated anchor events, antiquity to the present. Hand-authored context for the record rail (F7) and convergence detection, never generated content.

anchors.title: Cuneiform writing emerges at Uruk
anchors.summary: Temple accountants in Sumer press marks into clay; administration becomes memory that outlives the administrator.

anchors.title: The Great Pyramid rises at Giza
anchors.summary: Khufu's builders organize tens of thousands of laborers and rations on a scale no state had managed before.

anchors.title: Sargon founds the Akkadian empire
anchors.summary: The first durable multi-city empire yokes Sumer's rival temples to one crown and one road network.

anchors.title: Hammurabi publishes his law code
anchors.summary: Babylon carves prices, wages, and penalties in stone, law as public infrastructure.

anchors.title: The Bronze Age system collapses
anchors.summary: Within a generation the palace economies of the eastern Mediterranean burn or starve; trade, literacy, and cities retreat for centuries.

anchors.title: Iron-working spreads through the Near East
anchors.summary: Cheap iron loosens the bronze monopolies; farming and war both change hands.

anchors.title: The Phoenician alphabet takes shape
anchors.summary: Twenty-two letters a merchant can learn replace scripts only scribes could master.

anchors.title: The Zhou claim the Mandate of Heaven
anchors.summary: A new dynasty justifies conquest with a theory of legitimacy that will govern Chinese politics for three millennia.

anchors.title: First recorded Olympic games
anchors.summary: Greek cities begin counting years by a shared festival, a calendar of rivals.

anchors.title: Traditional founding of Rome
anchors.summary: A hill town on the Tiber begins the accumulation that will end as the Mediterranean's landlord.

anchors.title: Lydia mints the first coins
anchors.summary: Stamped electrum turns trust in metal into trust in the stamp; markets speed up accordingly.

anchors.title: Cyrus takes Babylon
anchors.summary: The Persian empire assembles the largest state yet seen and governs it with roads, satraps, and tolerance.

anchors.title: Cleisthenes reforms Athens
anchors.summary: Athenian citizenship is rewired around neighborhoods instead of clans; the demos becomes an institution.

anchors.title: The Buddha teaches in the Ganges valley
anchors.summary: A renouncer's answer to suffering begins its long migration across Asia.

anchors.title: Confucius wanders between courts
anchors.summary: A failed office-seeker's teachings on ritual and duty become East Asia's administrative ethic.

anchors.title: Greek fleets win at Salamis
anchors.summary: The Persian advance into the Aegean stalls in a strait; the Greek experiment keeps its independence.

anchors.title: The Peloponnesian war begins
anchors.summary: Athens and Sparta spend a generation demonstrating how rich democracies and disciplined oligarchies exhaust each other.

anchors.title: Alexander overthrows Persia at Gaugamela
anchors.summary: A Macedonian army ends the Achaemenid order; Greek becomes the administrative language from the Nile to the Indus.

anchors.title: The Library of Alexandria is endowed
anchors.summary: The Ptolemies pay scholars to collect, copy, and correct everything written in Greek, knowledge as state project.

anchors.title: Qin unifies China
anchors.summary: Weights, measures, axle widths, and script are standardized at sword-point; the imperial template is set.

anchors.title: Ashoka carves his edicts
anchors.summary: After the slaughter at Kalinga, the Mauryan emperor advertises remorse and dharma on pillars across India.

anchors.title: Hannibal destroys a Roman army at Cannae
anchors.summary: Rome loses perhaps fifty thousand men in an afternoon and, decisively, declines to negotiate.

anchors.title: Carthage is destroyed
anchors.summary: Rome erases its rival and inherits the western Mediterranean's trade whole.

anchors.title: Han envoys open the western routes
anchors.summary: Zhang Qian's missions link Chinese silk to Central Asian horses and, eventually, Roman silver.

anchors.title: Fire reaches the Library of Alexandria
anchors.summary: During Caesar's Alexandrian war, fire spreads from the docks and part of the library's holdings burn.

anchors.title: Caesar is assassinated
anchors.summary: The Republic's defenders kill the dictator and get, within twenty years, a permanent monarchy anyway.

anchors.title: Augustus founds the principate
anchors.summary: Rome's civil wars end in an emperor who insists he is merely first citizen; the fiction holds for centuries.

anchors.title: Cai Lun standardizes papermaking
anchors.summary: Rags and bark become a writing surface cheap enough for bureaucracy at scale.

anchors.title: The Antonine plague sweeps the Roman world
anchors.summary: Soldiers returning from the east carry a pandemic that hollows cities and armies for a generation.

anchors.title: The Han dynasty falls
anchors.summary: China fractures into three kingdoms; four centuries of division begin.

anchors.title: Constantine backs Christianity
anchors.summary: An emperor's battlefield vow moves a persecuted sect toward establishment.

anchors.title: Constantinople is dedicated
anchors.summary: Rome gets a second capital on the Bosporus, better placed for the empire's money and enemies alike.

anchors.title: Gupta India's court science flourishes
anchors.summary: Astronomers and mathematicians at Pataliputra work with a decimal notation the world will eventually borrow.

anchors.title: Alaric sacks Rome
anchors.summary: The city that had not fallen in eight centuries falls in three days; the shock outruns the damage.

anchors.title: The western Roman empire ends
anchors.summary: Odoacer retires the last western emperor; the office lapses with less noise than its idea will make for the next millennium.

anchors.title: The Justinianic plague arrives
anchors.summary: Yersinia pestis reaches the Mediterranean and returns in waves for two centuries, resetting labor and land.

anchors.title: Hagia Sophia is consecrated
anchors.summary: Justinian's dome outbuilds every church in Christendom and every engineer's caution.

anchors.title: The Grand Canal links China's rivers
anchors.summary: Grain from the Yangtze can now feed armies on the Yellow River; unification acquires plumbing.

anchors.title: The hijra to Medina
anchors.summary: Muhammad's community leaves Mecca; within a century its successors govern from Spain to Sind.

anchors.title: Arab armies win at Yarmouk
anchors.summary: Byzantine Syria falls in a week of battle; the Roman and Persian duopoly of the Near East ends.

anchors.title: Chang'an is the world's largest city
anchors.summary: Tang China's capital hosts perhaps a million people and every religion on the Silk Road.

anchors.title: Battle of Tours
anchors.summary: A Frankish shield wall checks a raiding army from al-Andalus; the Carolingians bank the prestige.

anchors.title: Baghdad is founded
anchors.summary: The Abbasids build a round city at the crossroads of the world's trade and begin paying for translations of everything.

anchors.title: Charlemagne is crowned emperor
anchors.summary: A pope revives the western imperial title on Christmas day; church and crown are entangled for a millennium.

anchors.title: The House of Wisdom flourishes
anchors.summary: Baghdad's scholars translate Greek, Persian, and Indian science into Arabic, and improve it.

anchors.title: The Great Heathen Army lands in England
anchors.summary: Scandinavian raiding turns to conquest and settlement; the North Sea becomes one rough economy.

anchors.title: The Song dynasty is founded
anchors.summary: China reunifies under a dynasty that will govern with examinations, paper money, and the world's largest iron industry.

anchors.title: Gunpowder formulas are published in China
anchors.summary: The Wujing Zongyao prints recipes for the mixture that will eventually rewrite every siege.

anchors.title: The Great Schism
anchors.summary: Rome and Constantinople excommunicate each other; Christendom's halves stop pretending.

anchors.title: The Norman conquest of England
anchors.summary: One October battle replaces England's ruling class, land law, and half its vocabulary.

anchors.title: The First Crusade takes Jerusalem
anchors.summary: Frankish armies storm the city and found crusader states the region will spend two centuries digesting.

anchors.title: Bologna's law school becomes a university
anchors.summary: Students hire their teachers and incorporate; the European university is born as a guild.

anchors.title: Temüjin becomes Genghis Khan
anchors.summary: The steppe confederates under one khan; within two generations his house rules from Korea to Hungary.

anchors.title: Magna Carta is sealed
anchors.summary: English barons force a king to concede that even he sits under law, a clause lawyers will quote forever.

anchors.title: The Mongols sack Baghdad
anchors.summary: The Abbasid caliphate ends in a week of slaughter; the Tigris runs with ink and blood alike, the chroniclers insist.

anchors.title: Marco Polo reaches Kublai's court
anchors.summary: A Venetian family's trade mission becomes Europe's best-selling description of a richer world.

anchors.title: Mansa Musa's hajj floods Cairo with gold
anchors.summary: Mali's emperor spends so freely en route to Mecca that Egyptian gold prices sag for years.

anchors.title: The Black Death reaches Europe
anchors.summary: Perhaps half of Europe dies within five years; wages, faith, and the feudal bargain never fully recover.

anchors.title: The Ming expel the Mongols
anchors.summary: A peasant rebel becomes emperor and rebuilds China's institutions around agrarian orthodoxy.

anchors.title: Zheng He's first treasure voyage
anchors.summary: Ming fleets larger than anything afloat carry the emperor's flag to India, Arabia, and Africa, then, within thirty years, are scrapped.

anchors.title: Agincourt
anchors.summary: English longbows and French mud embarrass chivalry; the war grinds on anyway.

anchors.title: Gutenberg completes the 42-line Bible
anchors.summary: Movable type proves itself at Mainz; the price of the written word begins its long collapse.

anchors.title: Constantinople falls to the Ottomans
anchors.summary: Mehmed II's guns end the Eastern Roman Empire; Greek scholars and their libraries scatter west.

anchors.title: Granada surrenders; Iberia expels its Jews
anchors.summary: The last emirate in Spain falls, and within months the expulsion edict scatters Sephardic life across the Mediterranean.

anchors.title: Columbus reaches the Caribbean
anchors.summary: Two hemispheres that had traded nothing begin exchanging crops, silver, empires, and diseases.

anchors.title: Da Gama reaches India by sea
anchors.summary: Portugal opens a spice route around Africa and prices the old caravans out.

anchors.title: Luther posts the ninety-five theses
anchors.summary: An indulgence dispute in Saxony becomes, via the printing press, the fracture of western Christendom.

anchors.title: Tenochtitlan falls
anchors.summary: Cortés, smallpox, and indigenous allies bring down the Mexica capital; New Spain rises on its ruins.

anchors.title: Babur founds the Mughal empire
anchors.summary: Field guns at Panipat win Delhi for a Timurid exile; his house will govern most of India for two centuries.

anchors.title: Copernicus publishes on the heavens
anchors.summary: A canon's deathbed book moves the Earth; the argument will take a century and several trials.

anchors.title: Silver is found at Potosí
anchors.summary: An Andean mountain begins bankrolling Spain and inflating prices from Seville to Beijing.

anchors.title: Lepanto
anchors.summary: A Holy League fleet checks Ottoman sea power in the last great galley battle.

anchors.title: The Spanish Armada fails
anchors.summary: Weather and gunnery break the invasion of England; Atlantic power starts drifting north.

anchors.title: Sekigahara decides Japan
anchors.summary: One morning's battle delivers Japan to the Tokugawa, who close and quiet it for 250 years.

anchors.title: The Dutch East India Company is chartered
anchors.summary: Amsterdam invents the joint-stock megacorporation, complete with shares, dividends, and a private navy.

anchors.title: Galileo publishes his telescope observations
anchors.summary: Moons around Jupiter and mountains on ours: the heavens acquire texture and the argument acquires evidence.

anchors.title: The Thirty Years' War begins
anchors.summary: A defenestration in Prague opens a war that will kill perhaps a third of the German lands.

anchors.title: The Peace of Westphalia
anchors.summary: Exhausted powers agree that sovereigns answer to no one above them; the modern state system gets its charter.

anchors.title: The Qing take Beijing
anchors.summary: Manchu banners ride through a rebel-opened gate; China's last dynasty begins.

anchors.title: The Royal Society is founded
anchors.summary: London gentlemen institutionalize the experiment: nothing by mere authority.

anchors.title: Newton publishes the Principia
anchors.summary: One set of laws for apples and planets; nature becomes calculable.

anchors.title: The Glorious Revolution
anchors.summary: England imports a king on conditions; parliament and public debt both become permanent.

anchors.title: England and Scotland unite
anchors.summary: One parliament, one market, one flag for the island that is about to run the seas.

anchors.title: Newcomen's engine pumps a mine
anchors.summary: Fire lifts water in Staffordshire, inefficiently, profitably, and portentously.

anchors.title: Plassey delivers Bengal to a company
anchors.summary: The East India Company converts a bribed battle into the revenues of a province, and then of an empire.

anchors.title: Watt's improved engine goes to work
anchors.summary: A separate condenser turns steam from a pump into a prime mover for anything.

anchors.title: American independence is declared
anchors.summary: Thirteen colonies secede on Enlightenment credit and win with French help.

anchors.title: Smith publishes The Wealth of Nations
anchors.summary: The division of labor gets its theorist; political economy becomes a discipline.

anchors.title: The French Revolution begins
anchors.summary: A bankrupt monarchy summons the estates and receives a nation instead; every European order takes note.

anchors.title: The Haitian revolution begins
anchors.summary: The enslaved of Saint-Domingue rise and, uniquely, win, founding a state and terrifying every slaveholding power.

anchors.title: Jenner demonstrates vaccination
anchors.summary: Cowpox against smallpox: the first standardized defeat of a disease begins.

anchors.title: The Louisiana Purchase
anchors.summary: France sells half a continent to fund a war; the United States doubles overnight.

anchors.title: Trafalgar
anchors.summary: Nelson's fleet settles a century's question: the seas are British.

anchors.title: Britain abolishes the slave trade
anchors.summary: The world's largest slaving power outlaws the traffic and sets its navy against it, slowly, and for mixed motives.

anchors.title: Spanish America begins its independence wars
anchors.summary: Napoleon's occupation of Spain snaps the imperial chain; juntas from Caracas to Buenos Aires stop waiting.

anchors.title: Waterloo and the Vienna settlement
anchors.summary: Napoleon's last army breaks; the powers redraw Europe for a century of managed balance.

anchors.title: Tambora erupts
anchors.summary: The largest eruption in recorded history yellows skies worldwide and cancels the next summer's harvests.

anchors.title: The first public railway opens
anchors.summary: Stockton to Darlington by steam: distance begins its long discount.

anchors.title: Morse telegraphs Washington to Baltimore
anchors.summary: News detaches from horses; markets and ministries synchronize by wire.

anchors.title: The Great Famine begins in Ireland
anchors.summary: Blight meets doctrine; a million die and two million leave while grain is exported under guard.

anchors.title: The 1848 revolutions sweep Europe
anchors.summary: Barricades from Paris to Vienna win constitutions in the spring that armies revoke by winter.

anchors.title: The Taiping rebellion begins
anchors.summary: A failed examination candidate's heavenly kingdom drags China into the deadliest civil war ever fought.

anchors.title: Perry's squadron enters Edo Bay
anchors.summary: Four American ships end Japanese seclusion by arithmetic of gun calibers.

anchors.title: Bessemer announces cheap steel
anchors.summary: Air blown through iron makes steel by the ton; rails, ships, and skylines follow.

anchors.title: The Indian rebellion of 1857
anchors.summary: Sepoy mutiny becomes general revolt; the Company is abolished and the Raj rules directly.

anchors.title: Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species
anchors.summary: Selection without a selector: biology acquires its unifying, unsettling theory.

anchors.title: Italy is proclaimed a kingdom
anchors.summary: Cavour's diplomacy and Garibaldi's volunteers stitch the peninsula together under Piedmont.

anchors.title: The Emancipation Proclamation
anchors.summary: The American civil war becomes, officially, a war against slavery.

anchors.title: The Meiji Restoration
anchors.summary: Japan's young oligarchs abolish their own class and industrialize the country in a generation.

anchors.title: The Suez Canal opens
anchors.summary: Europe and Asia move four thousand miles closer; whoever holds the ditch holds the route.

anchors.title: Germany is unified at Versailles
anchors.summary: Bismarck's wars end with a Prussian king crowned German emperor in a French palace.

anchors.title: Bell patents the telephone
anchors.summary: The wire learns to carry voices; conversation stops requiring presence.

anchors.title: Practical incandescent light
anchors.summary: Edison's filament and his grid make night optional for the paying public.

anchors.title: The Berlin conference partitions Africa
anchors.summary: European ministries rule lines across a continent most of them have never seen.

anchors.title: Koch isolates the tuberculosis bacillus
anchors.summary: Disease acquires identifiable causes; public health acquires targets.

anchors.title: Japan adopts the Meiji constitution
anchors.summary: Asia's first modern constitution, drafted to keep the oligarchs in and the powers impressed.

anchors.title: Röntgen photographs the invisible
anchors.summary: X-rays open the body to inspection without a knife and physics to a new century of surprises.

anchors.title: The Wright Flyer lifts at Kitty Hawk
anchors.summary: Twelve seconds of powered flight; the third dimension opens for traffic and war alike.

anchors.title: Japan defeats Russia
anchors.summary: An Asian constitutional power sinks a European empire's fleet; every colonized capital notices.

anchors.title: Haber fixes nitrogen from air
anchors.summary: Synthetic ammonia unlocks fertilizer and explosives in the same reaction; the world's food ceiling lifts.

anchors.title: The Qing dynasty falls
anchors.summary: A railway dispute becomes a revolution; two millennia of imperial rule end with a child's abdication.

anchors.title: The July Crisis becomes the Great War
anchors.summary: A murder in Sarajevo works through the alliance machinery; four empires enter the grinder.

anchors.title: The Bolsheviks take Petrograd
anchors.summary: War-broken Russia falls to the one party promising bread, land, and exit; the century acquires its schism.

anchors.title: The influenza pandemic
anchors.summary: The flu kills more than the war just ending, and is remembered less.

anchors.title: The Treaty of Versailles
anchors.summary: The victors redraw Europe and price the war onto Germany; the settlement satisfies no one who signs it.

anchors.title: Insulin saves its first patients
anchors.summary: A death sentence becomes a manageable condition within a single year of clinical work.

anchors.title: The Turkish republic is proclaimed
anchors.summary: From the Ottoman collapse, Mustafa Kemal builds a secular nation-state by decree.

anchors.title: Fleming notices penicillin
anchors.summary: A contaminated dish in a London lab holds the first antibiotic, unexploited for a decade.

anchors.title: The Wall Street crash
anchors.summary: Leverage unwinds; the Depression it triggers unseats governments and gold standards everywhere.

anchors.title: Hitler is appointed chancellor
anchors.summary: Germany's conservatives hand power to a movement they believe they can manage.

anchors.title: The Long March
anchors.summary: The Chinese communists retreat six thousand miles and emerge with a leader: Mao.

anchors.title: Germany invades Poland
anchors.summary: The European war resumes twenty years after its armistice, this time totally.

anchors.title: Pearl Harbor
anchors.summary: Japan staggers the US Pacific fleet and, in doing so, ends American neutrality everywhere.

anchors.title: The Wannsee conference coordinates the Holocaust
anchors.summary: Bureaucrats schedule genocide; six million Jews are murdered in the machinery that follows.

anchors.title: Stalingrad falls to the Soviets
anchors.summary: An army freezes and surrenders on the Volga; the eastern war reverses direction.

anchors.title: Bretton Woods designs the postwar economy
anchors.summary: Delegates in a New Hampshire hotel peg currencies to the dollar and invent the IMF and World Bank.

anchors.title: Atomic bombs destroy Hiroshima and Nagasaki
anchors.summary: Two cities end in two flashes; war acquires a ceiling and politics a new arithmetic.

anchors.title: The United Nations is chartered
anchors.summary: The victors institutionalize their alliance with a veto for each of them.

anchors.title: India and Pakistan become independent
anchors.summary: The Raj ends at midnight, partitioned; freedom and displacement arrive on the same trains.

anchors.title: The transistor is demonstrated
anchors.summary: Three men at Bell Labs replace the vacuum tube with a sliver of germanium; electronics begins shrinking.

anchors.title: Israel declares independence
anchors.summary: A state is proclaimed and immediately at war; the region's defining conflict takes shape.

anchors.title: The People's Republic of China is proclaimed
anchors.summary: Mao announces the new state from Tiananmen; the world's largest population changes systems.

anchors.title: The structure of DNA is published
anchors.summary: A double helix explains heredity's copying trick; biology becomes an information science.

anchors.title: The Bandung conference
anchors.summary: Twenty-nine African and Asian states meet without their former rulers and name themselves a third force.

anchors.title: The Suez crisis
anchors.summary: Britain and France seize the canal and are ordered out by Washington; the imperial era's end is invoiced.

anchors.title: Sputnik orbits
anchors.summary: A beeping sphere makes the sky political; the space race is on.

anchors.title: The Green Revolution takes hold
anchors.summary: Dwarf wheats and new rices double harvests across Asia; famine retreats where fertilizer reaches.

anchors.title: The year of Africa
anchors.summary: Seventeen colonies become states in twelve months; the UN's roster and the map both redraw.

anchors.title: The Cuban missile crisis
anchors.summary: Thirteen days at the edge; both superpowers glimpse the end and install a hotline.

anchors.title: The US Civil Rights Act
anchors.summary: A decade of marches and murders forces segregation out of American law, if not life.

anchors.title: The Cultural Revolution begins
anchors.summary: Mao turns China's youth against its institutions; a decade of upheaval consumes schools, temples, and cadres.

anchors.title: Apollo 11 lands on the Moon
anchors.summary: Six hundred million watch a footprint; the program that made it is cancelled within three years.

anchors.title: ARPANET's first message
anchors.summary: Two university computers exchange half a word; the network of networks begins.

anchors.title: The dollar leaves gold
anchors.summary: Nixon closes the gold window; money becomes, openly, a matter of policy.

anchors.title: The first oil shock
anchors.summary: An embargo quadruples oil prices; the postwar boom's cheap-energy floor gives way.

anchors.title: The last natural smallpox case
anchors.summary: A disease that killed three hundred million in its final century is hunted to zero.

anchors.title: Deng opens China's economy
anchors.summary: Household plots and special zones begin the fastest mass enrichment in history.

anchors.title: The Iranian revolution
anchors.summary: The shah flies out and the ayatollah flies in; political Islam takes state power.

anchors.title: IBM ships the PC
anchors.summary: Big Blue standardizes the desktop computer and, inadvertently, hands the profits to its suppliers.

anchors.title: Chernobyl
anchors.summary: Reactor four burns openly for days; the fallout reaches Sweden before the admission does.

anchors.title: The Berlin Wall opens
anchors.summary: A botched press conference ends the German partition; the bloc dissolves within two years.

anchors.title: The World Wide Web goes public
anchors.summary: A CERN side project gives the internet an address book and a face; publishing becomes a verb anyone can do.

anchors.title: The Soviet Union dissolves
anchors.summary: The flag comes down on Christmas night; fifteen states inherit the rubble and the warheads.

anchors.title: South Africa votes across race lines
anchors.summary: Apartheid ends at the ballot box; Mandela is inaugurated by the state that jailed him.

anchors.title: The human genome is drafted
anchors.summary: Three billion letters read once, expensively, then ever more cheaply, forever.

anchors.title: Polynesian navigators settle the remote Pacific
anchors.summary: Star paths and double-hulled canoes carry settlers across the largest ocean, island by island.

anchors.title: Maize is fully domesticated in Mesoamerica
anchors.summary: Millennia of selection turn a wild grass into the crop that will feed hemispheric civilizations.

anchors.title: Olmec centers rise on the Gulf coast
anchors.summary: Mesoamerica's first monumental culture carves colossal heads and sets templates its successors inherit.

anchors.title: Chavín de Huántar becomes an Andean pilgrimage center
anchors.summary: A highland temple complex knits scattered valleys into one ritual and trade sphere.

anchors.title: Nok culture smelts iron in West Africa
anchors.summary: Furnaces south of the Sahara work iron early and independently; the technology spreads with Bantu-speaking farmers.

anchors.title: Aksum dominates Red Sea trade
anchors.summary: An Ethiopian kingdom mints its own gold and brokers between Rome and India.

anchors.title: Teotihuacan at its height
anchors.summary: A gridded metropolis of a hundred thousand or more, ruling central Mexico without a named king history remembers.

anchors.title: Classic Maya cities flourish
anchors.summary: Dynasts at Tikal and Calakmul war and ally, while scribes keep the hemisphere's only full writing system.

anchors.title: Borobudur is completed in Java
anchors.summary: A mountain of carved stone terraces makes Southeast Asia's wealth and Buddhism visible for miles.

anchors.title: Angkor Wat is built
anchors.summary: The Khmer empire's hydraulic capital raises the largest religious monument on earth.

anchors.title: Great Zimbabwe at its height
anchors.summary: Dry-stone walls enclose a cattle-and-gold capital trading with the Swahili coast and beyond.

anchors.title: Timbuktu's manuscript culture flourishes
anchors.summary: Saharan trade underwrites libraries and jurists; books are the city's most durable export.

anchors.title: Korea prints with movable metal type
anchors.summary: The Jikji is printed decades before Mainz, the technique exists; the market and script differ.

anchors.title: The Inca road system spans the Andes
anchors.summary: Forty thousand kilometers of graded road and rope bridges run an empire without wheels or writing.

anchors.title: Tenochtitlan at its height
anchors.summary: Canals, causeways, and chinampas feed a lake capital larger than most European cities.

anchors.title: The Columbian exchange reworks world diets
anchors.summary: Potatoes and maize move east, wheat and cattle west, silver everywhere, and pathogens deadliest of all.

anchors.title: Coffeehouses open in Istanbul
anchors.summary: A new drink builds a new room, caffeinated, talkative, and repeatedly banned for it.

anchors.title: The Gregorian calendar reform
anchors.summary: Ten days vanish by papal bull; Europe spends three centuries disagreeing about what day it is.

anchors.title: The Atlantic slave trade nears its peak
anchors.summary: The plantation complex moves millions of Africans in chains; sugar and cotton price in the suffering.

anchors.title: Edo's townsman culture flowers
anchors.summary: A million-person city of clerks and craftsmen invents kabuki seasons, print celebrity, and takeout food.

anchors.title: The Encyclopédie begins publication
anchors.summary: Diderot's contributors put trades, machines, and heresies into alphabetical order for subscribers.

anchors.title: The Lisbon earthquake
anchors.summary: A capital falls on All Saints' morning; European philosophy takes the aftershock personally.

anchors.title: Cook charts the Pacific
anchors.summary: Three voyages map the ocean's last blank spaces, and open every island on them to empire.

anchors.title: Britain mandates smallpox vaccination
anchors.summary: The state requires a medical procedure of every infant; public health and civil liberty begin their long argument.

anchors.title: Pasteur patents pasteurization
anchors.summary: Gentle heat keeps wine, then milk, from souring; germ theory reaches the kitchen.

anchors.title: The US transcontinental railroad is joined
anchors.summary: A golden spike closes the gap at Promontory; the continent becomes a week wide.

anchors.title: Russia abolishes serfdom
anchors.summary: Twenty-three million people are unbound by decree, into redemption payments that last generations.

anchors.title: New Zealand grants women the vote
anchors.summary: The first national women's franchise; the precedent travels slowly but does not reverse.

anchors.title: The Panama Canal opens
anchors.summary: The isthmus is cut after forty years and twenty-five thousand deaths; two oceans share a lock.

anchors.title: Regular radio broadcasting begins
anchors.summary: A voice speaks to everyone in range at once; the mass audience becomes simultaneous.

anchors.title: Penicillin is mass-produced
anchors.summary: Deep-tank fermentation turns a lab curiosity into a war supply; bacterial infection loses its death grip.

anchors.title: Ghana leads sub-Saharan independence
anchors.summary: Nkrumah's Ghana leaves the empire first and hosts every liberation movement that follows.

anchors.title: The contraceptive pill is approved
anchors.summary: Fertility becomes a daily private decision; family size and workforces shift within a generation.

anchors.title: The first container ship sails
anchors.summary: A trucker's steel box collapses loading costs and, with them, the distance between factory and market.

anchors.title: Saigon falls
anchors.summary: Helicopters lift from a rooftop; the superpower loses the war and keeps the argument.

anchors.title: AIDS is first described
anchors.summary: Five case reports in Los Angeles announce a pandemic that will kill tens of millions before treatment arrives.

anchors.title: The Maastricht treaty founds the EU
anchors.summary: A common market votes itself a union, a citizenship, and, on a schedule, a currency.

anchors.title: Mobile phones reach the mass market
anchors.summary: The phone leaves the wall and the desk; presence and reachability quietly renegotiate.
